issues.detail: The Hebrew 'יִכְבָּד' (from כָּבֵד) means 'be heavy/weighty' or 'be honored/glorified' — the Chinese '得榮耀' (receive glory) is acceptable. However, the subject is ambiguous: 'מֵחוֹל יַמִּים יִכְבָּד' literally 'from the sand of the seas he/it will be heavy/honored' — the Chinese adds '祂' (He) as subject, which is not explicit in Hebrew but could be inferred. More critically, 'דְּבָרַי לָעוּ' means 'my words are swallowed up/come to nothing' (from לָעָה, 'to swallow'), not '已廢棄' (have been abolished/abandoned). The Chinese '已廢棄' implies deliberate rejection, whereas the Hebrew means they are 'swallowed up' or 'fade away' — a nuance of being overwhelmed, not abolished. This changes the sense from 'my words are overwhelmed' to 'my words are nullified'.
